mainTopic: Contradicting new-moon witnesses, the storekeeper and money changer cases, and רב and שמואל's rule that a person cannot pass an oath down to his heirs, with the challenges to it.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רב חסדא from a ברייתא about witnesses who disagree on the new moon's height. רבא explains that 'joining another testimony' means only another ראש חודש testimony, where it becomes two against one. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה's customer cases: רבי יהודה limits the oath to when the produce is still lying there, and the גמרא shows why the storekeeper case and the money changer case are both needed. Then the גמרא explains that orphans need an oath when they collect a debt from the borrower's orphans. רב and שמואל add that if the borrower died first, the lender's heirs cannot collect at all, because a person cannot pass an oath down to his children. רבי אלעזר disagrees, and רבי אמי tries to split the cases by whether the lender already stood in court. רב נחמן rejects that split and says the rule is all-or-nothing, a statement made within רבי מאיר's view. The rest of the amud brings משניות about a widow's heirs, a second wife's heirs, and a husband's heirs, all answered in line with רב and שמואל. A new challenge from רב נתן בר הושעיא begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about witnesses who disagree on the moon's height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a small disagreement about the moon's height does not cancel the testimony, but a large one does. Even then, the witnesses may still join another testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says the moon was two oxgoads high and the other says three, their testimony stands. If one says three and the other says five, their testimony is cancelled, but they can still join together with others for another testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for a challenge. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of one oxgoad is an easy mistake to make, so the testimony is still good. A gap of three to five is too big, so the testimony falls. The key line is the last one: each witness can still 'join another testimony.' The גמרא will use that line to challenge רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Oxgoads, the sticks used to drive oxen. Here they are a way to measure how high the moon looked above the horizon.
Their testimony stands and is valid.
Their testimony is cancelled.
They join together, so two witnesses count as one valid pair.

phrases.english: One witness says: it was two oxgoads high
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who came to בית דין to say they saw the new moon.

phrases.english: and the other one says: three
their testimony stands.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ –
phrases.english: If one says three and the other says five,
their testimony is cancelled,
but they can join together for another testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי מַרְדְּעוֹת וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about witnesses who contradict each other and about רב חסדא's view that such a witness is suspected.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that a witness who is contradicted is suspected of lying.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets contradicted witnesses join another testimony, which suggests they are not treated as suspected liars.

steps.title: Does 'another testimony' mean money cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'another testimony' means testimony about money. That would mean these witnesses are not suspected, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, doesn't it mean testimony about money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the challenge. It suggests the ברייתא lets these witnesses testify even in money cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a witness whose words were contradicted can still testify about money, then he is not treated as a suspected liar. That goes against רב חסדא. The word 'מאי לאו' marks a pushing question: 'Isn't it obvious that it means this?'

keyTerms.meaning: 'What, doesn't it mean...?' The גמרא uses this to suggest a reading that will cause a problem.
Testimony in a case about money.

phrases.english: What, is it not for testimony about money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the troubling reading out of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If contradicted witnesses can testify about money, they are not considered suspected liars, which is the opposite of רב חסדא's view.

steps.title: רבא: it means another new-moon testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'another testimony' means another testimony about ראש חודש. There, one of these witnesses joins a second witness, making two against one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He and another witness can join for another testimony about ראש חודש. They become two against one, and the words of one witness do not count against two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He reads 'another testimony' in a narrower way, so the ברייתא no longer goes against רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not talking about money cases at all. It means that a third witness comes and agrees with one of the two, so there are two against one. Two witnesses always beat one, so the one who disagreed falls away. This reading fits רב חסדא, because nothing here says the witness is trusted in other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The new month, which בית דין set based on witnesses who saw the new moon.
Two against one.

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: The words of one witness carry no weight against two.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, 'join another testimony' in the ברייתא means another testimony about ראש חודש, where it becomes two against one. It does not mean money cases, so רב חסדא's view stands.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He and another witness can join together
phrases.notes: 'He' means one of the two witnesses who disagreed about the moon's height.

phrases.english: for another testimony about the new moon;
because then they are two against one,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and the words of one have no weight where there are two.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הוּא וְאַחֵר מִצְטָרְפִין לְעֵדוּת אַחֶרֶת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's words 'another testimony'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Another testimony' means any testimony, including money cases, which would show that a contradicted witness is not suspected.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Another testimony' means a new-moon testimony where he joins with another witness to form two against one, so רב חסדא is not contradicted.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the customer and the storekeeper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a customer who asked a storekeeper for a דינר's worth of produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If someone said to a storekeeper, 'Give me produce for a דינר,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the opening words of a case in the משנה. This step sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the storekeeper gave the produce. Then the two argue over whether the customer paid. The משנה's ruling is that the customer swears that he paid.

keyTerms.meaning: A storekeeper.
A coin of a certain value.
'And so on.' The rest of the משנה is not quoted here.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לַחֶנְוָנִי ״תֵּן לִי בְּדִינָר פֵּירוֹת״ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If he said to a storekeeper: 'Give me produce for a dinar,' and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the witness discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the משנה's dispute over payment, the customer swears that he paid.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the customer's oath
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה's view. The customer swears only while the produce is still piled in front of them. Once he has taken it away on his back, the storekeeper must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, when does this apply? When the produce is piled up and lying there, and both of them are arguing over it. But if the customer has slung it in his basket on his back, the one who wants to take from his friend must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה adds a limit to the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the produce is still lying in the store, the two sides are equal, so the customer swears. Once the customer has picked up the produce and carried it off, he is holding it. Now the storekeeper is the one trying to take money from him, so the storekeeper must prove his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Piled up and lying there, still in the store.
Arguing or making claims about something.
He slung them, meaning he put them on his back.
Whoever wants to take something from another person must bring the proof.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that holding the item changes who has to bring proof. It is a basic rule found all over the laws of money.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When does this apply?
phrases.notes: He's asking when the משנה's rule applies, that the customer swears and doesn't pay.

phrases.english: When the produce is piled up and lying there,
and the two of them are arguing over it;
but if he slung it in his basket behind his back,
the one who wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יהודה's limit to the משנה case quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The customer swears only while the produce is still lying there. Once he has carried it off, the storekeeper must bring proof.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs the money changer case too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's money changer case and begins explaining why both cases are needed. The storekeeper case alone would not teach the money case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If someone said to a money changer, 'Give me,' and so on. Both cases are needed. If the משנה had taught only the first case, we would say that only there do the רבנן rule this way. That is because produce tends to spoil, and since it spoils, storekeepers do not hold on to it. But coins do not spoil, so you might say the רבנן agree with רבי יהודה there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second case in the משנה and starts a צריכותא, which explains why the משנה teaches two cases that look alike. Here it shows why the storekeeper case alone is not enough. The other half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With produce, the customer's claim makes sense: a storekeeper hands produce over quickly before it spoils, even before he is paid. Coins do not spoil, so a money changer has no reason to hand them over before he is paid. So without the money changer case, we might think the רבנן agree with רבי יהודה there, and the customer would not be able to swear.

keyTerms.meaning: A money changer, who gives small coins in exchange for a large one.
'And it is needed.' This opens a צריכותא, which explains why two cases are both needed.
They rot or spoil.
They do not hold on to it; they hand it over right away.
Agrees with, concedes to.

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the first half of the צריכותא. It explains why the storekeeper case does not teach the money changer case. The other direction, why the money changer case alone is not enough, comes next.

phrases.english: If he said to a money changer: 'Give me,' and so on.
And both cases are needed;
for if it had taught us only this first case,
phrases.notes: The 'first case' is the storekeeper and the produce.

phrases.english: we would say that only in that case do the Rabbis rule this way,
phrases.notes: The רבנן are the ones in the משנה who say the customer swears and does not pay.

phrases.english: because produce tends to spoil,
and since it spoils, they do not hold on to it;
but with coins, which do not spoil,
you might say they agree with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יהודה's limit, the גמרא explains why the משנה needs both the produce case and the money case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the storekeeper case alone, we might think that with coins, which do not spoil, the רבנן agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money changer case teaches that the רבנן's ruling applies to coins too. The other half of the צריכותא follows.

steps.title: Finishing why both cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the money changer case, we might think רבי יהודה agrees with the רבנן in the storekeeper case. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only the money changer case, I would say רבי יהודה rules this way only there, but in the storekeeper case he agrees with the רבנן. So both cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation it started in Step 6. It shows the other side: the money changer case alone would not teach the storekeeper case either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that the storekeeper case alone would not teach the money case. Now the גמרא shows the reverse: from the money changer case alone, we might think רבי יהודה agrees with the רבנן about the storekeeper. Each case teaches something the other cannot, so the משנה needs both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. The גמרא's word for showing that two cases are both needed.
Agrees, admits the other side is right
The Sages, the majority view against רבי יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה teaches something the other could not. That is why both are written.

phrases.english: And if it had been stated only about that case
phrases.notes: "That case" is the money changer case, and "this case" in row 3 is the storekeeper.

phrases.english: I would say that only in that case does Rabbi Yehuda rule this way

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּהָךְ אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן;
phrases.english: but in this case, say that he agrees with the Rabbis
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation begun in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that each of the two cases is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the money changer case, we would think רבי יהודה agrees with the רבנן in the storekeeper case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases must be taught, because רבי יהודה disagrees in both.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about orphans collecting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of people who collect only with an oath, including orphans.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: just as the Sages said that a woman who lessens her כתובה collects only with an oath, and so on, likewise orphans collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה about orphans. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases where someone collects only after swearing. The גמרא focuses on the orphans case, because it is not clear whom the orphans are collecting from.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who admits she already received part of her כתובה
Orphans, the heirs of someone who died
They collect payment

phrases.english: Just as they said
a woman who lessens her marriage contract, etc.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'etc.', isn't in every version. It just means the quote is cut short and the משנה goes on.

phrases.english: and likewise, the orphans may not collect.
phrases.notes: The משנה finishes: they may not collect except with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, unrelated to the storekeeper discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans collect only by taking an oath.

steps.title: From whom do the orphans collect?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom the orphans collect from. If it means the living borrower, it makes no sense that the father collected without an oath but his orphans need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From whom do they collect? If you say from the borrower himself, that makes no sense. Their father would collect without an oath, and they need an oath?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means, and shows that the simple reading has a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lender with a document collects from the borrower without swearing. The orphans should not be worse off than their father. So the משנה cannot mean that orphans need an oath to collect from the borrower himself.

keyTerms.meaning: From whom?
The borrower
If you say. This brings in a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject.

phrases.english: From whom?
If you say from the borrower,
their father takes payment without an oath,
and they need an oath?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The simple reading of the משנה, that orphans need an oath to collect from the borrower
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heirs should not have a weaker claim than their father, and the father collected without an oath.

steps.title: Orphans collecting from orphans
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means orphans collecting from the borrower's orphans. In that case they need an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: likewise, orphans collecting from orphans collect only with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining which case the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides have died: the lender and the borrower. Someone who collects from orphans must swear, so the lender's orphans need an oath as well.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to explain what a text is really saying.
Orphans collecting from orphans

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
and likewise, orphans collecting from orphans
may not collect except with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which case the משנה is talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The orphans collect from the living borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: The orphans collect from the borrower's orphans, and for that they need an oath.

steps.title: רב and שמואל: only if the lender died first
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל say this rule applies only when the lender died first. If the borrower died first, the lender already owed an oath, and he cannot pass that oath to his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: this was taught only when the lender died while the borrower was alive. But if the borrower died while the lender was alive, the lender already had to swear to the borrower's children, and a person cannot pass an oath down to his children.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל limit the משנה's rule to one order of deaths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower died first, the lender himself would have needed to swear in order to collect from the borrower's orphans. His children cannot swear in his place about something only he knew. So according to רב and שמואל, they cannot collect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of. Used to limit a rule.
The lender
A person cannot pass down an oath to his children

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the children's oath is too hard to take. It means the debt itself is lost, because only the father could have sworn the oath needed to collect it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limit is what רבי אלעזר is asked about and disagrees with in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both say:
They taught this only
where the lender died during the lifetime of the borrower;
but if the borrower died during the lifetime of the lender,
the lender has already become obligated
to take an oath to the borrower's children,
and a person does not pass down an oath to his children.
phrases.notes: He means the children can't swear in their father's place, so they can't collect the debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule explained in Step 10 to a case where the lender died first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Orphans collect with an oath only if the lender died first. If the borrower died first, the lender's heirs cannot collect.

steps.title: Asking רבי אלעזר about this oath
steps.stepSummary: The question about רב and שמואל's ruling is sent to רבי אלעזר: what kind of oath is this?
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent it to רבי אלעזר: this oath, what is its nature?
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages send רב and שמואל's ruling to רבי אלעזר and ask him to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are asking how an oath that only the father owed can stop his children from collecting the debt altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent it, meaning they sent the question in a letter
What is its nature?

phrases.english: They sent it before Rabbi Elazar:
This oath, what is its nature?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning of רב and שמואל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why an oath the father owed should cancel his children's right to collect.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: heirs swear and collect
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back to them: heirs swear the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that the lender's children can collect after taking their own kind of oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes against רב and שמואל. The heirs do not need to swear their father's oath. They swear the oath that heirs swear, and that is enough to collect.

keyTerms.meaning: The heirs' oath
They take, meaning they collect

phrases.english: He sent to them:
Heirs swear the heirs' oath,
phrases.notes: The heirs' oath is that their father never told them the debt was paid.

phrases.english: and collect.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לְהוּ: יוֹרְשִׁין נִשְׁבָּעִין שְׁבוּעַת יוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12 by disagreeing with רב and שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lender's heirs take the heirs' oath and collect, even if the borrower died first.

steps.title: רבי אמי prepares to say something
steps.stepSummary: The question is sent again in the days of רבי אמי. He wonders why they keep asking, but agrees to say something about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent it again in the days of רבי אמי. He said: they keep sending this question so much? If we had found a reason, wouldn't we have sent it to them?! But רבי אמי said: since it came to us, let us say something about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The question comes up again, and רבי אמי prepares to give his own explanation. This sets up his statement, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי first complains that they would have answered already if they had a reason. Still, he decides to say something, and that statement opens the next part of the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: So much, to this extent
A reason, an explanation
Since it came into our hands
A word, something to say

phrases.english: They sent it in the days of Rabbi Ami.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כּוּלֵּי הַאי שָׁלְחִי לַהּ וְאָזְלִי?
phrases.english: He said: They keep sending it this much?
If we had found a reason for it,
wouldn't we have sent it to them?!
But Rabbi Ami said:
Since it has come into our hands,
let us say something about it:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same question is sent again, and רבי אמי prepares to address it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי prepares to give his own explanation of the oath.

steps.title: רבי אמי splits the cases by whether they already stood in court
steps.stepSummary: If the case was already heard in court before the lender died, the heirs cannot collect. If it was not yet heard, the heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the lender stood trial and then died, he was already obligated to swear to the borrower's children, and a person cannot pass an oath to his children. If he died before standing trial, his heirs take the heirs' oath and collect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives the answer he promised in step 14. He makes room for both earlier opinions by splitting the case into two situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל said the heirs lose, and רבי אלעזר said the heirs swear and collect. רבי אמי says each is right in a different case. If the court already ruled that the lender must swear, and he died before swearing, that personal oath dies with him. If the court never got involved, the heirs just take their own heirs' oath.

keyTerms.meaning: stood trial, meaning the case was already heard in court
the lender
the borrower
passing down an oath as an inheritance
the heirs' oath: 'Our father never told us this was paid'

phrases.english: If he stood trial and died,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the lender. He came to court against the borrower's children, then died before swearing.

phrases.english: the lender has already become obligated
to take an oath to the borrower's children,
and a person cannot pass down an oath to his children.
If he did not stand trial and died,
the heirs take the heirs' oath,
and collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of רבי אמי's answer, which step 14 introduced
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to fit together רב and שמואל's ruling and רבי אלעזר's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After a trial, the oath was personal and cannot be inherited. Before a trial, the heirs swear the heirs' oath and collect.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the court does not create the oath
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that the lender owed the oath from the moment the borrower died, whether or not he went to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objects: Is it the court that makes him owe an oath? From the moment the borrower died, the lender already owed an oath to the borrower's children!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רבי אמי's split. He says standing in court changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי's split assumes the oath only becomes 'his' once a court rules. רב נחמן says the duty to swear began when the borrower died, because the lender could only collect from orphans with an oath. So the lender always owed the oath before he died, and the split falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: objects to it (a strong challenge)
is that to say...? (introduces a doubtful assumption)
the court
from the moment

phrases.english: רב נחמן objects to this:
Is that to say that the court
is what makes him obligated to take an oath?!
From the moment the borrower died,
the lender became obligated
to take an oath to the borrower's children!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's split between before trial and after trial
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's split based on standing in court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The obligation to swear starts when the borrower dies, not when the court rules. So the lender always owed the oath before he died, and the court case makes no difference.

steps.title: רב נחמן: either accept רב and שמואל or don't
steps.stepSummary: Instead of splitting cases, רב נחמן says רב and שמואל's rule is all-or-nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: If the ruling of רב and שמואל stands, it stands. If it does not, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked down רבי אמי's split, רב נחמן gives his own position. There is no middle ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the court case makes no difference, רב and שמואל's rule must apply to every case where the borrower died first, or to none. רב נחמן does not say which way he holds. That gap sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: it exists, meaning the ruling is accepted
it does not exist, meaning the ruling is not accepted

phrases.english: Rather, רב נחמן said:
If the ruling of רב and שמואל is accepted, it is accepted;
if it is not accepted, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי אמי's split with an all-or-nothing approach
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and שמואל's rule applies everywhere or nowhere. It cannot depend on whether the case reached court.

steps.title: But רב נחמן ruled in a real case that they divide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב נחמן sounds unsure, but a report says he ruled in an actual case against רב and שמואל's approach.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he is unsure about it? But didn't רב יוסף בר מניומי say: רב נחמן ruled in an actual case that they divide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רב נחמן's words as doubt. It then challenges that reading from a report of how he actually ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'if it stands, it stands' sounds like someone who has not decided. But a real ruling of 'they divide' shows that רב נחמן had a clear position, and it went against רב and שמואל's approach. So how can he be unsure?

keyTerms.meaning: evidently / so it seems
he is uncertain about it
ruled in an actual case
they divide (the disputed money)

phrases.english: Evidently, he is uncertain about it;
but didn't רב יוסף בר מניומי say:
רב נחמן ruled in an actual case:
They divide!
phrases.notes: This is the case where neither side can be trusted to swear. רב נחמן had them split the money instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלמא מספקא ליה והאמר רב יוסף בר מניומי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt that seems to be in רב נחמן's statement
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב נחמן is undecided
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real ruling of 'they divide' shows that רב נחמן had a clear position against רב and שמואל's approach, so he could not be unsure.

steps.title: He spoke according to רבי מאיר, but did not hold that way himself
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's 'if it stands' was said within רבי מאיר's view, which רב and שמואל follow. His own view is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was speaking according to רבי מאיר's view, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רב נחמן's doubt was only inside someone else's system.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל's rule fits רבי מאיר's approach. רב נחמן was saying that within רבי מאיר's view, the rule is all-or-nothing. In practice he follows a different view, which is why he ruled 'they divide.'

keyTerms.meaning: according to the words (view) of
he does not hold that way

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not contradicting himself. His 'if it stands' statement works inside רבי מאיר's system. His real ruling, 'they divide,' follows his own view.

phrases.english: He was speaking according to the view of רבי מאיר,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the statement was made within another תנא's system
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן himself was unsure about רב and שמואל's rule
steps.terutzMaskana: He was describing how the rule works within רבי מאיר's view. He personally rules otherwise, that they divide.

steps.title: רב אושעיא challenges from a widow's heirs collecting her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says a widow's heirs can claim her כתובה for up to 25 years. This seems to show heirs collecting even though she never swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא challenges: If she died, her heirs can bring up her כתובה for up to twenty-five years!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא raises a source against רב and שמואל. A widow must swear before collecting her כתובה, yet her heirs still collect after her death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow owed an oath to her husband's heirs. If she died without collecting, רב and שמואל would say her oath cannot pass to her children. Yet the משנה lets her heirs collect, which contradicts רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: bring up / claim
the marriage contract payment owed to a wife

phrases.english: רב אושעיא challenges:
If she died, her heirs
phrases.notes: 'She' is a widow who hadn't yet collected her כתובה (משנה in כתובות 104a).

phrases.english: may bring up her כתובה
for up to twenty-five years!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב and שמואל's core rule
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and שמואל's rule that a person cannot pass down an oath to his children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The widow owed an oath and died. Her heirs still collect from orphans, so it seems the oath obligation did pass to her children.

steps.title: The widow had already sworn before she died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a widow who took her oath and then died before collecting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where she swore and then died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אושעיא by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the widow already swore, nothing is left for her heirs to swear. They are only collecting money already proven owed. So no oath is being inherited, and רב and שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with here? (a standard way to narrow a source)
that she had sworn

steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל: someone who owed an oath and died without swearing cannot pass that oath to his heirs. רבי אמי's split based on standing in court is rejected by רב נחמן. The widow's case is explained as one where she had already sworn.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
Where she swore and then died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The widow died without swearing, and her heirs collected anyway
steps.terutzMaskana: She swore before dying, so no oath needed to pass to her heirs.

steps.title: The second wife's heirs collect first
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that when a man dies, his second wife and her heirs collect her כתובה before the heirs of his first wife. This seems to show heirs collecting money that needed an oath, even though their mother never swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A man married a first wife and she died. Then he married a second wife, and he died. The second wife and her heirs come first, before the heirs of the first wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה to challenge רב and שמואל. That משנה lets the second wife's heirs collect her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow who collects her כתובה from her husband's estate must take an oath first. The משנה lets the second wife's heirs collect, which suggests that even if she died before swearing, her heirs can still collect. That seems to go against רב and שמואל, who say an oath cannot be passed down to heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: The first wife
The second wife
Come first; have priority

phrases.english: Come and hear:
He married a first wife, and she died;
he married a second wife, and then he died —
the second wife and her heirs come first,
before the heirs of the first wife!
phrases.notes: The first wife's sons have a claim to her כתובה money too. The משנה puts the second wife's heirs ahead of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge from a משנה, built the same way as the challenge in Step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב and שמואל that an oath cannot be passed down to heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second wife's heirs collect a כתובה that needed an oath, which suggests heirs can collect even if their mother never swore.

steps.title: Here too, she swore before she died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about a second wife who already took her oath and only then died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the case is where she swore and then died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge the same way it answered in Step 21: the wife swore first and only then died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wife has sworn, she already has a full right to collect. Her heirs are not inheriting an oath. They are only inheriting money she had already earned the right to collect. So the משנה does not go against רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same answer as before
That she took the oath

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: This is the same answer the גמרא gave in Step 21.

phrases.english: it is where she swore and then died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to include a wife who died before swearing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only talking about a wife who swore before she died, so nothing was left to pass down except the money.

steps.title: The husband's heirs can make her heirs swear
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says the husband's heirs can make the wife, her heirs, and those acting for her swear. Her heirs swearing seems to mean they inherited her oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: But his heirs can make her swear, and her heirs, and those who come on her behalf!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה from כתובות to challenge רב and שמואל again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the husband agreed not to make his wife swear. Still, his heirs can make her swear, and also her heirs. If her heirs swear and then collect, it looks like the oath was passed down to them, and that goes against רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Make someone take an oath
His heirs (the husband's heirs)
Those who come on her behalf, such as people acting for her

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in כתובות (86b). The husband had agreed not to make her swear.

phrases.english: But his heirs can make her swear,
and her heirs, and those who come on her behalf!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge from a different משנה, after Step 23 answered the previous one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב and שמואל that an oath cannot be passed down to heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has the wife's heirs swearing and collecting, which seems to show that her oath was passed down to them.

steps.title: Two separate cases: widow and divorcée
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה explains that the משנה describes two separate cases. A widow swears herself. Her heirs swear only in the case of a divorcée who died while her ex-husband was still alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: The משנה is teaching two separate cases. 'Her' means a widow. 'Her heirs' means a divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה answers the challenge by splitting the משנה into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the widow case, the husband died first, so she herself swears to his heirs, and nothing is passed down. In the divorcée case, she died while her ex-husband was still alive. At that time she owed no oath, because he had agreed not to make her swear. When he died, the duty to swear to his heirs started fresh with her heirs, so it was not inherited from her.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches separate cases: each part of the list belongs to a different situation
Widow
Divorcée

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as one case where both the wife and her heirs swear. רב שמעיה's whole point is that each one belongs to a different situation.

phrases.english: רב שמעיה said:
It is teaching separate cases:
'her' — in the case of a widow;
and 'her heirs' — in the case of a divorcée.
phrases.notes: He means a divorcée who died before her ex-husband did, so she herself never owed his heirs an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24 by reading the משנה as two separate cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source into separate cases (לצדדין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife and her heirs both swear in the same situation, so her heirs seem to inherit her oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her heirs swear only in the divorcée case, where they owe a new oath of their own and did not inherit hers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when heirs swear, it does not always mean they inherited an oath. Sometimes the duty to swear starts fresh with them.

steps.title: A son's power can be greater than his father's
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר הושעיא starts a new challenge from a ברייתא that says a son's power is sometimes greater than his father's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר הושעיא raised a challenge: The power of the son is greater than the power of the father —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. רב נתן בר הושעיא begins quoting a ברייתא, and the rest of it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line hints that a son can sometimes collect in a situation where his father could not. This will be used against רב and שמואל, but the full case has not been quoted yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The son's power is greater (stronger)
The father's power

phrases.english: רב נתן בר הושעיא raised a challenge:
The power of the son is greater than the power of the father —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 25 answered the last challenge, a new challenge begins from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רב and שמואל that an oath cannot be passed down to heirs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a son can sometimes collect where his father could not, that seems hard to fit with heirs losing their claim just because their father died before swearing. The full argument continues on the next amud.
